questions.question: 1. In which of the following is the interference due to the division of wavefront?

answers.b: Demonstration of colours of thin film

explanations.a: Correct: YDSE uses division of wavefront — a single wavefront is divided at two slits.
explanations.b: Incorrect: Thin film colours arise from division of amplitude (partial reflection).
explanations.c: Incorrect: Lloyd's mirror is classified under division of amplitude.
explanations.d: Incorrect: Fresnel's biprism also uses division of wavefront, but YDSE is the primary textbook example.

questions.question: 2. If a torch is used in place of monochromatic light in Young's experiment, what will happen?

answers.a: Fringes will appear for a moment then disappear
answers.c: Only bright illumination will appear (no distinct fringes)
answers.d: Fringes will occur exactly as from monochromatic light

explanations.a: Incorrect: Fringes will not be stable even momentarily due to mixed wavelengths.
explanations.b: Incorrect: There will be light on the screen, but without a clear fringe pattern.
explanations.c: Correct: Multiple wavelengths wash out the interference pattern, leaving overall bright illumination.
explanations.d: Incorrect: Polychromatic (white) light cannot produce sharp stable fringes.

questions.question: 3. The fringe width in YDSE is doubled if:

answers.a: The wavelength of light is doubled

explanations.a: Doubling λ doubles β because β ∝ λ.
explanations.b: Doubling D doubles β because β ∝ D.
explanations.c: Halving d doubles β because β ∝ 1/d.
explanations.d: Correct: Any one of these independent changes will double β.

questions.question: 4. In Young's double slit experiment, the condition for the formation of a dark fringe is: path difference =

explanations.a: Incorrect: nλ is the condition for bright (constructive) fringes.
explanations.b: Incorrect: λ/2 is only the n=0 case; the general condition is (2n+1)λ/2.
explanations.c: Correct: Dark fringes form when path difference = (2n+1)λ/2, i.e., an odd multiple of λ/2.
explanations.d: Incorrect: (n+1)λ gives another bright fringe, not a dark one.

questions.question: 5. If the path difference between two coherent light waves is λ/2, what type of interference occurs?

explanations.a: Incorrect: λ/2 path difference corresponds to a 180° phase shift — cancellation, not addition.
explanations.b: Correct: Path difference = (n + ½)λ = λ/2 for n = 0 gives destructive interference.
explanations.c: Incorrect: Interference still occurs; it is just destructive.
explanations.d: Incorrect: Maximum intensity requires path difference = nλ, not λ/2.

questions.question: 6. In YDSE, the position of the n-th dark fringe on the screen is given by

explanations.a: Incorrect: This is the position of the n-th bright fringe.
explanations.b: Correct: Dark fringes occur at half-integer multiples: yₙ = (n + ½)λD/d.
explanations.c: Incorrect: The screen distance D is missing from this expression.
explanations.d: Incorrect: This gives a different set of positions and is not the standard form.

questions.question: 7. Two coherent sources are 0.3 mm apart and 1 m away from the screen. The second dark fringe is at 0.3 cm from the centre. What is the distance of the 4th bright fringe from the centre?

explanations.a: Incorrect: 0.6 cm corresponds to the 3rd bright fringe.
explanations.b: Correct: Fringe width β = 0.2 cm; 4th bright fringe position = 4 × 0.2 = 0.8 cm.
explanations.c: Incorrect: 1.2 cm would correspond to the 6th bright fringe.
explanations.d: Incorrect: This is far smaller than the actual fringe spacing.

questions.question: 8. In YDSE, what happens to the fringe width if the experiment is performed in water (refractive index μ > 1)?

explanations.a: Incorrect: Fringes do not vanish simply because the medium changes.
explanations.b: Incorrect: μ > 1 reduces the wavelength in the medium, so fringe width shrinks.
explanations.c: Correct: λ' = λ/μ, so β' = λD/(μd) = β/μ, which is smaller.
explanations.d: Incorrect: Changing the wavelength through the medium always changes β.

questions.question: 9. In YDSE, if one slit is completely closed, what will be observed on the screen?

answers.a: Interference fringes with half the intensity

explanations.a: Incorrect: Closing one slit destroys the two-slit interference pattern entirely.
explanations.b: Correct: With only one slit open, light undergoes single-slit diffraction.
explanations.c: Incorrect: Light still passes through the open slit and produces a diffraction pattern.
explanations.d: Incorrect: Closing a slit reduces, not doubles, the pattern complexity.

questions.question: 10. The central fringe in Young's double slit experiment is always

explanations.a: Incorrect: The path difference at the centre is zero, giving maximum — not minimum — intensity.
explanations.b: Incorrect: With monochromatic light the central fringe is not coloured.
explanations.c: Correct: Path difference = 0 at the centre satisfies constructive interference for any wavelength.
explanations.d: Incorrect: The central bright fringe is the brightest and most visible fringe.
